ratings.concept: Superior versus inferior ovary: china rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, onion and tulip are hypogynous, guava and cucumber epigynous
ratings.reason: This question requires one remembered flower fact for each of eight named plants, demonstrated by the stem's "china rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, guava, cucumber, onion and tulip", whose ovary positions cannot be worked out from anything else in the question.
ratings.note: No trap is written, and the candidates were these: mis-filing brinjal as epigynous because the fruit sits on a persistent calyx gives five, and adding tulip to that gives four. Neither lands securely, because nothing printed in the stem or the options says which of the eight was mis-filed - any one of them produces five and any two produce four. The three wrong options are simply counts one, two and three below the key, so an option cannot be tied to a particular route and the list is left empty.

ratings.concept: Pleiotropy: a single gene controlling several unrelated traits, as in phenylketonuria and sickle-cell anaemia

traps.label: semantic_reversal
traps.route: Turns the relation round: many genes acting on one trait instead of one gene acting on many. That is complementary gene action.

traps.label: look_alike_term
traps.route: Hears "pleio-" as "Pliocene" and answers with a geological date.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: Nothing in the term fixes a plant group. Pleiotropy counts how many traits one gene affects and says nothing about which organisms carry it.

ratings.reason: This question requires holding two neighbouring genetic terms apart, demonstrated by option 4's "Controls a trait only in combination with another gene", which states the reverse relation to option 1's "Controls multiple traits in an individual".

group_note: Five of the six are plain_mcq; q089 is the exception, because its stem is only the instruction "Select the wrong statement:" and each option is a complete claim with no lettered block printed above them, which section 1 sends to statement_options. q090 was not sent there even though its options also complete a trailing stem: "A pleiotropic gene:" names its subject, so the content does not live entirely in the options. Format follows the options alone and splits on one test - a bare noun phrase naming a thing is name_or_identify (q086, q087, q088), a complete claim graded true or false is pick_correct_statement (q089, q090), a tally is count_qualifying_items (q085). Demand is recall in five members: each is settled by stored facts, whether one (q087, q088) or one per option (q085, q086, q089). q090 alone is concept_discrimination, because its option set turns on telling pleiotropy from complementary gene action rather than on retrieving either. Solution structure follows the same split: single_step where one fact about the keyed option decides it, several_independent_checks where every option or every listed item has to be graded - eight plants in q085, four claims in q086 and q089. Traps are uniform only where the question makes them so: q086 and q089 are negated, so their wrong options are true statements failing the polarity and all three in each carry true_statement_trap. Elsewhere each wrong option got the device it actually carries, which is why q090 has three different labels. Two members hold back: q085 carries no trap at all, because the wrong options are counts one, two and three below the key and nothing printed says which plant was mis-filed, and q088 leaves option 3 untagged because no bacterial structure is tied to growth. Both are explained in their notes rather than covered with a near-fitting label.
